content.content: {"result":"{\"documentId\": \"f_1326e66bcabfda8fd29e4a\", \"title\": \"Close-out register conventions\", \"name\": \"Close-out register conventions\", \"revisionId\": \"8b9413d402\", \"createdTime\": \"2026-02-13T16:38:02Z\", \"modifiedTime\": \"2026-02-13T16:58:40Z\", \"text\": \"Close-out register conventions\\n1. One row per vendor account. If the same vendor shows up twice (two issues, two names), it's one row under the name on its invoice, and the newer issue is the duplicate.\\n2. Leave out people, contractors and professional firms (legal, accounting, Sunset), taxes and filing services, insurance, bank fees, one-off purchases, anything the company itself never paid for, and anything cancelled before Feb 9. Exception: anything on Sunset's list goes on the register whatever else applies.\\n3. Arthur's project came from the P&L and our lists; he skipped one-off, filing and insurance lines and ones long gone. AWS and the ad accounts in the UA line stay off the register: he and I are closing those out ourselves. Before you call it complete, add what it misses inside any other costs-tab line that covers several vendors \\u2014 each account there gets its own row.\\n4. What we do: Cancel, Keep (my keep list, as amended in the thread), Move to Arthur's LLC (his card), or Hold for Sunset. Sunset's list wins over everything above.\\n5. Where it stands, for Cancel rows only: Closed = the vendor itself has confirmed (their email, an in-app or bot notice, a final invoice) \\u2014 say where. Requested = one of us has cancelled or asked but nothing has come back from the vendor. Open = nobody has done anything yet. Leave it blank on the other rows.\\n6. By when: for Cancel rows that aren't Closed, the day before the next charge (for accounts billed on usage \\u2014 ads, cloud \\u2014 use Feb 28), or the SVB card on the founders' board if it sets an earlier date. For Keep and Hold rows still charging the SVB card while we need them, follow SVB's card terms. Hold rows already off that card, or that won't charge it again before Sunset's review call, stay until the review call; Keep rows that aren't on the SVB card get a dash. Moved and Closed rows get a dash, unless an export or a switch-over still has to happen before the access ends \\u2014 then the day before it ends.\\n7. Owner: the Linear assignee unless the issue hands it to someone else. Anything you add is yours.\\n8. Monthly cost, rounded to cents: the monthly figure its owner gives in its Linear issue, or else its own last invoice or receipt brought to a month (annual \\u00f7 12, quarterly \\u00f7 3). Free plans and accounts that have never charged us are 0.\\n9. Two totals at the bottom: the sum of the monthly cost column over every row (what it all costs us today), and the same sum over the Keep and Hold rows only (what's left after the plan).\\n10. A clash is a decision one of us already posted in #winddown that Sunset's list or SVB's card terms would undo. Moving who pays for an account isn't one (it closes nothing), and requests or suggestions aren't decisions.\\n\"}"}

1. One row per vendor account. If the same vendor shows up twice (two issues, two names), it's one row under the name on its invoice, and the newer issue is the duplicate.

10. A clash is a decision one of us already posted in #winddown that Sunset's list or SVB's card terms would undo. Moving who pays for an account isn't one (it closes nothing), and requests or suggestions aren't decisions.

Hi Leonard, Robert, Arthur,

Thanks for signing today. Before we can deliver the licensed data set, these accounts need to stay active with their full history and every user in place until we confirm delivery: Slack (stay on the paid plan — the free plan hides history older than 90 days), Google Workspace (every user account, including former staff — please don't archive or delete any), Figma, Linear, GitHub and Metabase. Nothing on this list should be closed, downgraded or archived before the delivery review call Leonard booked with us. Accounts that aren't on the list aren't part of the licensed bundle, so close them whenever suits you.

For Helpshift, please export the full ticket history to Drive before your subscription ends.

If our engineers change anything on this list, we'll reply on this thread.

Best,
Maya
Client onboarding, Sunset
====
Hi all — one change after our engineers walked through your data map today: Trello is part of the bundle too, and Metabase isn't (it only reads from BigQuery), so please keep BigQuery and dbt instead. The rest of the list stands.

Maya
====

We have unfortunate news. Harmony Games Inc. is shutting down and preparing to file for dissolution.
Because of this, we need to terminate our agreement with Singular effective immediately. Unfortunately, the company is insolvent and we have no cash reserves left, There are no funds available to pay any remaining balance.
We have valued the relationship and the team at Singular. We have not come close to using the plan, we have spent well under 1% of our ad spend cap, and we would appreciate your help in making this a clean, mutual early termination so we can properly close down without leaving obligations on your books.
Please confirm in writing that the contract and any related renewals are cancelled as of today, and let us know what you need from us to close the account and stop any further charges. I’m writing to share a difficult update: we have decided to wind down harmonygames.
We reached this decision after a thorough review of the most recent data across our products and the realistic set of options in front of us. Despite multiple iterations, we did not get the metrics to a point that supports a viable business path, and we do not have the funding to continue operating while searching for a new direction.
What we did and what we learned
• We built and tested three games on a limited budget, staying true to our mission of hybridcasual gameplay with RPG depth.
• We took real creative risks and pushed to innovate:
Domino Delights: Domino/Tripeak solitaire gameplay with RPG elements
Zombie Match 3D: Match Factory style core loop with RPG combat/progression elements
Combo Fighter: Tetris-like block gameplay with RPG elements
• We also explored partnerships and other paths to scale distribution and improve outcomes, but none changed the trajectory enough.
Financial context
• We have been in sustained financial hardship since mid-2025.
• Revenue did not reach meaningful levels, and the plans we pursued to change that did not work.
• Given our current runway of less than a month and obligations, continuing would create risk without a responsible probability of success.
What happens next
• We are initiating an orderly wind-down process and preparing the required board resolutions and documentation.
• Our priorities are to handle employee and contractor obligations properly, meet tax and compliance requirements, close out vendor commitments, and Sunset the products in a controlled way.
• We will also evaluate what to do with the remaining IP and codebase (archive, sale, or other disposition) and will keep you informed.
Timeline and updates
• We will share a more detailed wind-down plan and timeline shortly, including key dates for operational shutdown.
• I will send periodic updates as we complete the major steps and once we have clarity on final liabilities and any remaining assets.
I regret having to send this. I am proud of the team we put together and the quality of what we shipped. We ran a frugal operation, made multiple bets, and pushed hard, but we did not reach the performance required to build a durable company.

Register's done and shared with you and Arthur as editors: https://docs.google.com/spreadsheets/d/1LEDmkKp4KSPmq5L1ELhQFic9nIg7Pyjn4t1eHPx-XvM/edit (25 rows, built per your conventions doc)

**Monthly totals**
• Every row (what it all costs us today): **$6,706.49/mo**
• Keep + Hold rows only (what's left after the plan): **$1,249.04/mo**

**Clashes with what we already decided**
1. **Google Workspace**: the plan was to archive accounts on Google after Feb 15. Sunset's checklist says every user account, former staff included, stays, with nothing archived or deleted before the Mar 12 review call. So the archive has to wait until after Mar 12.
2. **Slack**: on the 11th you went with keeping only ~3 paid accounts and turning everyone else into guests (after the free-plan idea). Sunset needs Slack on the paid plan with full history and every user in place until Mar 12. So no seat cuts or downgrade before then.
Nothing else clashes. Arthur moving GitHub, dbt and Metabase to his card only changes who pays. Carta keeps its August date, since you exempted it on the SVB card.

**Linear**
• 6 Done (vendor confirmed): Helpshift, Zapier, Layer, Kapwing, Cursor, Soundly
• 4 Canceled: Google Ads (UA ad account you're closing yourself), Lucidchart (cancelled Oct '25), iPostal (mailbox closed Jan 16), Intuit (duplicate of QuickBooks)
• The rest stay open. Each issue has a comment saying what happens, by when and who owns it.

**Heads-ups for EOD Feb 17 (the SVB card closes on the 18th)**
• Off the SVB card by then: Slack, Google Workspace and QuickBooks
• Still waiting on written confirmation: Unity, Singular and CodeRabbit
• Not cancelled yet: Gusto, DocuSign (mine), 1Password and ElevenLabs
• ElevenLabs is the one I added. It sits inside the costs-tab "Sound" line ($50/yr Starter), so it's mine. Pond5 from the same line already ended in Sep.
• Sunset swapped Metabase out for BigQuery + dbt + Trello yesterday. Metabase now just goes to Arthur's LLC.

content.text:
The close-out register is built and shared with Leonard and Arthur as editors. All 28 Linear issues are settled with a comment on each, and I've replied in Leonard's #winddown thread with the totals and clashes.

**Register:** [Account close-out register](https://docs.google.com/spreadsheets/d/1LEDmkKp4KSPmq5L1ELhQFic9nIg7Pyjn4t1eHPx-XvM/edit), 25 rows, built per Leonard's conventions doc. It's in your Drive because Drive wouldn't let me move it into the Wind Down folder.

**The two monthly totals (in the reply):**
- **All rows (what everything costs today): $6,706.49/mo.** Unity ($2,348.50) and Singular ($2,083.33) are about two-thirds of it.
- **Keep + Hold rows (what's left after the plan): $1,249.04/mo.**

**Clashes I flagged:**
1. **Google Workspace:** Leonard planned to archive accounts after Feb 15. Sunset's checklist says no user account, including former staff, gets archived or deleted before their review call on Mar 12.
2. **Slack:** on Feb 11 Leonard decided to keep about three paid seats and turn everyone else into guests. Sunset needs the paid plan, full history and every user in place until Mar 12.

**Linear:**
- **Done (6):** the vendor confirmed the cancel for Helpshift, Zapier, Layer, Kapwing, Cursor and Soundly.
- **Canceled (4):** Google Ads (an ad account Leonard is closing himself), Lucidchart and iPostal (both ended before Feb 9), and Intuit (same account as QuickBooks).
- **Open:** everything else. Each issue has a comment saying what happens, by when and who owns it.

**Judgment calls you may want to know:**
- Sunset's later email swapped Metabase out and added BigQuery, dbt and Trello. GitHub and dbt are already on Arthur's card, but because they're on Sunset's list they're marked "Hold for Sunset" until Mar 12. Metabase is marked "Move to Arthur's LLC" and stays open in Linear, since a move isn't a close.
- I counted Layer as confirmed based on Leonard's screenshot of Layer's in-app notice in #prototype. CodeRabbit stays "Requested" because I couldn't find any confirmation from CodeRabbit.
- ElevenLabs had no Linear issue. It was hidden inside the P&L's combined sound-tools line, so I added it, and under Leonard's rules anything I add is yours.

**On your plate by end of day Feb 17** (the SVB card closes Feb 18, and Leonard wants every cancellation done by then):
- **DocuSign:** Leonard handed it to you. It's $300 a year and renews Apr 20.
- **ElevenLabs:** $50 a year Starter plan, renews Jul 9.
- **Figma:** you own it, but there's nothing to do. It's paid through Sep 11 and is held for Sunset until Mar 12.
